newsitem.title: UK: UK pension fund switches within Fleming Group.
newsitem.headline: UK pension fund switches within Fleming Group.

text.p: The 50 million stg pension fund of Britain's Avon County Council has been switched within the Fleming Group, partly because of a change of strategy by the client, a spokesman for Robert Fleming said.
The pension fund assets have been moved from Jardine Fleming in Tokyo to Robert Fleming, which owns 50 percent of the fund management group, in London.
Jardine Fleming in Hong Kong has been hit by client defections after a high-profile scandal involving illicit dealing by fund manager Colin Armstrong.
The spokesman said the company never discussed or commented on client business but added that the Tokyo operation had not been affected by events at Jardine in Hong Kong.
"In fact, it has seen some 550 million stg of new business coming in since then," the spokesman added.

No comment was immediately available from Bath and North East Somerset Council which now oversees the Avon County Council fund but industry sources said the Jardine saga had dented confidence and trustees wanted the fund managed closer to home.

Separately a British newspaper reported that a former director of Jardine Fleming in Hong Kong is to form an action and pressure group similar to that organised by Lloyds names, to fight for compensation after losses in the fund managed by Armstrong.

Bill Glover started Hong-Kong based Matheson PFC in 1975 and became chairman in 1989. He told the Evening Standard newspaper he knew of some 50 individuals who had money in JF Pacific Securities Trust and who blamed Armstrong for their losses.
